description:
Found by s532c (s536, 2026-11-08) while reducing #4623.  PRE-EXISTING (identical on 1191fa1a = MAIN-READY-72).
The compiler forces a STATIC forced-main glob into main (`\*STDIN` in package Foo emits
`(p-make-typeglob "main" "STDIN")`, s532b #4163 `Pl::Environment::forced_main_name`), but a SYMBOLIC one
lowers to `(p-dynamic-typeglob "STDIN")`, and the runtime qualifies a bare name with the CURRENT package.
Reproducer (perl 5.40.3: `2 main main main main` / `3 noio foo-has`; PCL: `2 Foo Foo Foo Foo` / `3 io foo-not`):
    package Foo; no strict 'refs';
    print "2 ", *{"STDIN"}{PACKAGE}, " ", *{"ENV"}{PACKAGE}, " ", *{"INC"}{PACKAGE}, " ", *{"ARGV"}{PACKAGE}, "\n";
    print "3 ", (defined *{"Foo::STDIN"}{IO} ? "io" : "noio"), " ", (exists $Foo::{STDIN} ? "foo-has" : "foo-not"), "\n";
Row 3 is the same family the other way: a QUALIFIED `Foo::STDIN` is a distinct glob in perl (no IO), and PCL
reaches the real STDIN (the handle resolver strips the qualifier; cf. #1423's open half,
`open(*Foo::STDOUT, ...)` closing the real STDOUT).  Printing through `*{$n}` with `$n = "STDOUT"` works
(the resolver reads the name).  Start: the bare-name qualification in `p-dynamic-typeglob`'s name
resolver -- one forced-main set for the runtime (s532c's `%p-main-std-handle-p` holds the handle half:
STDIN STDOUT STDERR ARGV ARGVOUT; gv.c's list adds ENV INC SIG `_`, and `%p-select-glob-name` keeps an
inline copy of the eight) -- probe `*{"SIG"}`, `*{"_"}`, `*{"main::STDIN"}` too.  Probe file:
scratch/s532c/p/dyn1.pl in the s532c worktree.

=== DONE (s536h) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, commit b5ef48dd; cl/ + one non-emitting Pl/Environment.pm accessor).  %p-glob-dynamic-name -- the ONE reading every dynamic-glob entry point shares (p-dynamic-typeglob, p-glob-assign-dynamic, p-local-glob-dynamic, p-glob-defined) -- qualifies an UNQUALIFIED name into main when %p-forced-main-bare-p says so: gv.c S_find_default_stash = one of the forced-main names, or a name that does not begin like an identifier (punctuation, a digit, a caret name, the empty name).  `package Foo; *{"STDIN"}{PACKAGE}` / ENV / INC / ARGV / SIG / _ / STDERR / STDOUT / ARGVOUT / "!" / "0" / "/" are main, "Other" / "stdin" / "INCX" stay Foo, `"" . *{"STDIN"}` is *main::STDIN (probed 5.40.3, identical).  ONE runtime list +p-forced-main-names+ (the inline copy in %p-select-glob-name now reads it); the compiler's list is Pl::Environment's @FORCED_MAIN, exposed as forced_main_names(), and Pl/t/forced-main-sub-01.t row 5 asserts the two are EQUAL (one fact in two languages).  %p-main-std-handle-p keeps its five names: a different fact (the handles whose IO the runtime keeps in its own state), and Pl/Binder.pm's %SPECIAL_MAIN is s536e's region (noted, not touched).  Guard rows 4-5 (FAIL on the base).  NOT fixed: row 3 of the filing (`*{"Foo::STDIN"}{IO}` is a distinct glob with no IO in perl, PCL reaches the real STDIN because the handle key interns into Foo and inherits :pcl's STDIN) = #1423's remaining (qualified-handle) half.
subject: `*{"STDIN"}` / `*{"ENV"}` / `*{"INC"}` / `*{"ARGV"}` inside `package Foo` build Foo's glob -- perl forces those names into main (`*{"STDIN"}{PACKAGE}` is main, PCL answers Foo)
